body:
release.sh bumps web/package.json (line 122) but not web/package-lock.json, whose top-level "version" is still 0.0.0 (last touched in July). Any `npm install` rewrites the lockfile's version to match package.json and dirties the tree — seen on this checkout. With AGENTS.md's warning about `git add -A` sweeping release leftovers, this is a live hazard: the next agent to run npm install and commit would carry the lockfile change into an unrelated commit.

Fix: have release.sh update the lockfile's two version fields as well (or run `npm version --no-git-tag-version` / `npm install --package-lock-only` in web/ after the edit), and reconcile the current lockfile to 1.16.0 in the same commit. Consider a check in verify-all.sh or release.sh that package.json and package-lock.json agree.
title: release.sh bumps package.json but not package-lock.json; npm install dirties the tree
